p: A bit of planning goes a long way at trampoline parks. Most venues ask for a waiver to be filled in online before you arrive, so do it at home and save yourself a queue at the desk. Hang on to your grip socks afterwards, as they can often be reused on your next visit, which saves a few quid. Lockers are handy for phones and keys, and it's worth bringing a bit of change or checking how they work before you go in.

Safety-wise, the usual trampoline rules apply: one person per trampoline, no double bouncing, and follow the instructions from the staff in the hall. Little ones are often best suited to quieter sessions, so look at the timetable if you're bringing toddlers or very young kids.

Once you've finished, Birmingham has loads of options that suit a tired but happy crew. Sea Life Birmingham by the canals at Brindleyplace is a good family follow-up with sharks, rays and otters. The Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square has a rooftop garden with city views, and Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery is well worth a look for its huge collection.

If the sun is out, Cannon Hill Park is a great spot for a run-around and a picnic, with boating lakes and plenty of space, and the Birmingham Botanical Gardens in Edgbaston are a calmer finish to the day. Hungry? The Jewellery Quarter has a great choice of independent cafés and restaurants.
